firmware.title: Bluetooth Firmware Selection
firmware.invalid: %s is not a Realtek firmware file: probably a web page was saved instead of the file. Download it again with the 'plain' link and replace it.
firmware.manual_instructions:
1. Click 'Open Download Page' to open kernel.org
2. Download the fw and config files
3. Click 'Open Config Folder' and place the files there
firmware.vendor_intel: Intel adapter (experimental): no Realtek files needed. If it starts in bootloader mode, place the matching ibt-*.sfi and ibt-*.ddc files from linux-firmware (intel/) in the config folder. AX210 and newer are not supported yet.
firmware.vendor_broadcom: Broadcom adapter (experimental): no Realtek files needed. It runs on its ROM firmware; optionally place a PatchRAM file such as BCM20702A1-0b05-17cb.hcd in the config folder.
firmware.vendor_csr: CSR adapter: no firmware files needed.
firmware.non_realtek: Realtek initialization is skipped. The adapter runs on its own firmware.
firmware.auto_no_adapter: No adapter detected. Bind it to WinUSB with Zadig; Auto then picks the chip when it is connected.
firmware.auto_unrecognized: The adapter was not recognized. If it has a Realtek chip, choose the chip; otherwise choose Not Realtek.
firmware.vendor_unsupported: This adapter needs a firmware loader that A2DPWB does not have (MediaTek / Qualcomm). It may not work.

advanced.max_packet_help:
Upper limit for the audio data in each Bluetooth packet (%d-%d). The headphones' own limit (MTU) always applies too; A2DPWB uses the smaller of the two.

%d (recommended) fits one Bluetooth baseband packet. Larger values save only 1-2%% overhead, but more audio is lost when a packet is lost. Applies from the next connection.

quality.title: Link Quality
quality.not_streaming: Not streaming. Values appear while audio is being sent.
quality.codec_capped: — limited by the device's maximum bit rate
quality.theory_value: %.0f kbps max, %.1f%% used (3-DH5 back to back)
quality.band_help: Packets occupy 1, 3 or 5 slots whatever their size, so radio time used is higher than the bandwidth share. Above about 80% little room is left for retransmissions and interference easily causes dropouts; lower the quality or turn on ABR in that case.
quality.loss_help: Packets are dropped before sending when the send queue is full (the radio cannot keep up) or L2CAP refuses them. Retransmissions over the air happen inside the Bluetooth controller and are not shown here.

dbgc.audio_stalled: Audio captured but no packets sent in the last second

receiver.title: Peer Receiver Test
receiver.intro: Streams to tools/linux_sink/a2dpwb_sink.py on another PC (Linux, ordinary Bluetooth adapter) and compares what was sent with what arrived. The receiver is found on the local network.
receiver.address_hint: empty = find on the local network
receiver.address_tooltip: IP address or host name of the PC running a2dpwb_sink (optionally :port). Empty: find it on the local network (UDP broadcast, port 51201).
receiver.searching: Looking for a receiver on the local network...
receiver.state_failed: Sending failed: %s Check the distance to the receiver and press Start again.
receiver.state_ready: Ready. Start sends to the receiver's Bluetooth adapter.
receiver.state_connecting: Connecting to the receiver over Bluetooth...
receiver.state_waiting: Waiting for audio to arrive at the receiver...
receiver.mtu_tooltip: MTU the receiver offers for the media channel: 672 as BlueZ, 679 the smallest LDAC accepts, 895 / 1005 common in headphones. Applies from Start.
receiver.log_start: Start: send %s, %s, %s, %s, %s to %s; receiver MTU %s, buffer %s
receiver.log_configure_failed: the receiver did not confirm the settings (older a2dpwb_sink?)
receiver.source_tooltip: Test tone (1 kHz left / 1.5 kHz right) keeps the stream steady. System audio sends what the PC plays; while it plays nothing, nothing is sent, and the receiver counts that as a pause.
receiver.afh_tooltip: Channels Bluetooth should avoid (AFH host classification, applies to every connection): Auto = the 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi channel this PC is connected on (nothing when it is not on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi), Off = leave it to the Bluetooth controller, Manual = the Wi-Fi channels entered, e.g. 6,11. At least 20 of the 79 channels stay in use.
receiver.help: Counts start with each stream and at Reset. Lost = gaps in the RTP sequence numbers (classic aptX and aptX LL carry none). The receiver models a sink with the buffer shown: a dropout is when it would have run dry, a skip when a burst after a stall would have overfilled it.

capture.app_hint: Lists the apps that are playing audio. If yours is missing, start playback in it and click Refresh.
capture.hint_loopback: Records what the Windows default output device plays: all apps mixed. It keeps playing on that device too.
capture.hint_virtual: Records what apps play into the selected device.
capture.hint_app: Records only what the selected app (and its child processes) plays, after the app's own processing. The app keeps playing on its output device too.
tooltip.codec: Audio codec for Bluetooth streaming. LDAC offers the highest quality.
tooltip.quality: Encoding quality level. Higher quality uses more bandwidth.
tooltip.abr: Adaptive Bit Rate: auto-adjusts quality based on connection stability (LDAC and LHDC V5). LHDC V5 ABR stays at 400 kbps or below (as on Android) and ignores the quality setting.
tooltip.codec_fallback: When the device does not offer the chosen codec, connect with the best codec it offers (as Auto does) instead of stopping with an error.
tooltip.le_audio: Stream to this device with LE Audio (BAP unicast, LC3) instead of A2DP. Codec, quality, sample rate and bit depth do not apply; A2DPWB picks the best LC3 configuration the device offers.
tooltip.codec_fallback_help:
The device did not offer %s when connecting, so %s is used instead.

Sony headphones (e.g. WH-1000XM4): LDAC is not offered while "Connect to 2 devices simultaneously" (multipoint) is on. Turn it off in the Sony Sound Connect (Headphones Connect) app, then connect again. Some models, such as the WH-1000XM6, support LDAC together with multipoint.

If the headphones are also connected to a phone or another PC, disconnect them there and connect again.
tooltip.sample_rate: Audio sample rate. Higher rates improve quality but use more bandwidth. Auto matches system output.
tooltip.bit_depth: Audio bit depth. 24-bit provides higher dynamic range (LDAC and LHDC V5).
volume.label: Volume
tooltip.volume: Headphone volume (AVRCP absolute volume). It also follows the volume buttons on the headphones, and the Windows volume chosen in the profile's Windows Volume Sync. Shown when the headphones support it.
tooltip.audio_device: Select the virtual audio device to capture from.
tooltip.auto_switch: Automatically set this device as the Windows default output when streaming.
tooltip.volume_sync: While streaming, this Windows volume and the headphones' volume follow each other. Auto: the device the audio is captured from (the default output device in System Loopback and Application mode). Choose Off if this volume also changes the captured audio, e.g. an effects app's own virtual device as the default output, or the volume is applied twice.

ui.adapter.none_hint: Plug in a USB Bluetooth adapter, then press Refresh. A2DPWB needs its own adapter, separate from the PC's built-in Bluetooth.
ui.adapter.assign_explain: A2DPWB drives the adapter itself through the WinUSB driver (part of Windows). While it is assigned, Windows' own Bluetooth no longer sees this adapter: devices paired with Windows through it stop working until you restore the driver. Other Bluetooth adapters (for example the PC's built-in one) are not affected.
ui.adapter.assign_short: Windows' Bluetooth will no longer use this adapter
ui.adapter.restore_title: Give the adapter back to Windows
ui.adapter.restore_explain: Windows picks its own driver for the adapter again, and Windows' Bluetooth can use it. A2DPWB cannot stream through it until WinUSB is assigned again.
ui.adapter.restore_short: Restore driver gives the adapter back to Windows' Bluetooth

ui.setup.title: Set up A2DPWB
ui.setup.intro: Four steps to hear your PC in your headphones.
ui.setup.adapter_intro: A2DPWB streams through its own USB Bluetooth adapter. Choose the one to use.
ui.setup.driver_ok: The adapter is ready for A2DPWB
ui.setup.device_intro: Put the headphones in pairing mode, scan, and choose them. A profile stores the device and the sound settings; the defaults give the best sound.
ui.setup.test_intro: Choose what to send to the headphones (all PC audio, a virtual device or one app), connect, and play something on the PC. If you hear it in the headphones, setup is done.
ui.setup.tone_playing_hint: Lower tone left, higher tone right: if that is what you hear, setup is done.
ui.setup.tone_failed: The test tone could not be played (%s). Connect with the profile instead and play something on the PC.
